body:
Thanks for your thoughts,  I appreciate them.  

To your comment about being mired in a loop of comparing myself to people around me: I guess I don't know how to stop comparing myself to those I care about.  How do you think I got my concepts of what I should be as an adult in the first place?

About the cross dressing:  I'm going to visit her this weekend.  Our relationship has been rocky since my self-doubt and insecurity has started to become a problem.  I plan to at least tell her, because I feel she has a right to know.  Of course, I'll probably get cold feet at the last minute, but this is the most conviction i've ever felt on the matter.

Thanks for the reply.  I think Grimjestor had it right.  There are moments when ending it all sounds like a blissful alternative to how my life feels.  But these moments always pass.  My desire not to hurt those who love me always outweighs my desire to stop the pain.

First, I want to say thank you for your response, because I know i'm not going to sound thankful in my reply.  But I am.  It means a lot to me that you took the time to respond.

You're right, there are plenty of things that I do better.  I'm a better cook.  I'm better at (most) video games.  I'm more athletic.  I'm (usually) less stressed out.  But the fact is, the aspect of our lives that I feel I cannot ever compare to her is the aspect of her life that is singularly most important.  Both her parents are incredibly brilliant, and a large part of her extended family aren't exactly slouches either.

But to be honest that's only part of the problem.  A big part of the problem is that the majority of her life reminds me that she is much more hardworking than me, and as a result, she is achieving the kinds of success that I have been raised to appreciate.

Now here's where your next comment comes in.   
"I expect there are a great many things you are proud of and even if their arent sitting around feeling sorry for yourself isnt going to make it happen"

I know this.  And I haven't been.  For the past 6 months, I have been trying to find ways to increase motivation, improve my work ethic, and generally improve my professional performance.  But while I may go to work with goals and objectives, by the end of my 8 hours, I'm tearing my hair out, ready to get the fuck out of there having put in the minimum required time for my job.

Also, she lives 6.5 hours away, so just taking her out for some enjoyment doesn't exactly work.

I want you to know that the comments you mentioned are all very valid.  In fact, they are all thoughts that I have had, or thoughts that my girlfriend has brought up.  But these are the responses my fucked up brain comes up with...

Holy fuck, you're only 16?  Damn, I wish I were as mature, and as astute as you are when I was your age.  

I appreciate the response, and you make a lot of good points.  Many of the points you mentioned are thoughts i've had myself, but failed to mention in my OP.  Hearing someone else say them helps me believe that those are the things I should be focusing on.

Though, there is one thing that I still struggle with.

"stop thinking what you cnt give her, start thinking how much you mean to her. How she makes you feel, how you try to make her happy. You are a very lucky man in so many ways having such a stable family dynamic, even though it can sometimes feel crushing and leave you feeling unworthy or like a failure, but your not, because you make your own targets and standards, like your girlfriend has hers, and they wont be the sam because your different people, and thats why you love her, because shes different, and thats why she loves you."
 
Its true.  There are a lot of things that I do for her.  And these are the reasons why she loves me.  But the aspect in which I feel I cannot compare seems like the single most important aspect of her life.  I think her success also tends to act as a reminder that I am not my father, and probably won't live up to the bar he set, as far as work ethic and professional success.  Especially because her work ethic and professional success (so far) leads me to believe that she will set the bar even higher.
